name: Ilford SFX 200
notes: EXTENDED RED SENSITIVITY film: the sheet says sensitivity extends to 740 nm (aimed at deep red filters) and that it also has full panchromatic sensitivity; coated on a grey acetate base. The spectral curve runs about 355-772 nm, with a broad plateau (about 0.6-0.8) from 400 to 720 nm and a fall at 725-770 nm.

Spectral sensitivity (page 1): 'Wedge spectrogram to tungsten light (2850K)' drawn as line curves on a 'Sensitivity' axis with ticks 0.5 and 1.0 only. Two curves are plotted, 'Conventional film' (a reference curve of a normal panchromatic film, peak 1.0 near 570 nm, cut at about 650 nm, NOT traced) and 'SFX 200', traced as sensitivity/v with the numbers as printed (relative, linear or log not stated; the frame bottom is about -0.08 on that scale). Below about 385 nm the two curves touch and the trace follows the merged line there (about 0.02 error); the leader lines and labels were masked.

Characteristic curve (page 2): x axis is RELATIVE log exposure (frame 0 to 4.5, no absolute lux-seconds, no Log H Ref), y is density, frame bottom = 0 (gridlines every 0.5, labelled 1.0 and 2.0). Densitometry type is not stated; balance 'daylight' is the light of the ISO 200/24 speed rating ('to daylight', measured in ID-11 at 20C).

One curve only: SFX 200 in ILFORD ID-11 stock for 10 min at 20C, intermittent agitation. Traced as v; base+fog about 0.29 as read, the curve ends at relative log exposure about 4.35 with density about 2.3. This curve is graphically identical to the one on the Delta 400 sheet (same numbers to about 0.01), so the same artwork was probably reused; it is not a measurement specific to SFX 200 with certainty.
No document code (footer 'Page n of 6, Nov 2018'), no granularity figure.
